name: Close the books each month (equipment finance company)
summary: Each month the accounting team closes the books of a lessor with about 55,000 contracts and $1.5 billion of leases and loans funded through conduits and a bank line. Lease accountants and ledger clerks reconcile the lease subledger, bank accounts, securitisation debt and other balances to the ledger, post accruals and the loss allowance, and the reporting analyst drafts statements that the controller and the chief financial officer review before they go to planning, treasury and the lenders. The close takes about eight business days because most reconciliations are in spreadsheets, differences between the lease system and the ledger have to be traced contract by contract, and figures from treasury, funders and the credit loss calculation arrive part-way through.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent lessor reporting under IFRS, with a lease management system feeding a mid-market ERP ledger, spreadsheet reconciliations and monthly lender and conduit reporting.
baseline.notes: One case is one monthly close. Hands-on minutes on each step are the combined hours of the people doing it; much of the work runs in parallel on business days 1 to 5.

trigger: The last business day of the month and the cut-off of postings in the lease system and the ledger.
end_state: Reconciliations are signed off, the period is locked and approved financial statements (with quarter-end schedules at quarter end) are delivered to planning, treasury, tax and the auditors.

volume.seasonality: Quarter ends add lender, board and auditor schedules; the year-end close is longer and feeds the annual audit.

evidence.note: One close a month, as in the organisation file.

Cost from the organisation file: Job Bank 2023-2024 Ontario wage for financial auditors and accountants (median $40.87) at about 90% for 2019-2022, loaded by 1.35. Six lease accountants also run lease and credit loss accounting, so about 1.2 FTE on the close is an author estimate.
Cost from the organisation file (accounting clerks, median $25.00 in Ontario, times 0.9 and 1.35). Four clerks; about 0.6 FTE on close reconciliations and cut-off is an author estimate.
Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Two managers; review, approvals and coordination.
Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Two analysts; trial balance, variance analysis and statements.
Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Review time plus close oversight.
Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Final review.
Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Occasional funding reconciliation support.

systems.name: General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires
Data warehouse and business intelligence reports

steps.name: Confirm cut-offs and the close calendar
steps.description: On the last business day the accounting manager re-sends the close calendar and checklist, confirms with operations, treasury, tax and HR that bookings, payouts, write-offs, fundings and payroll for the month are in, and reminds teams of the cut-off times for the lease system and the ledger.

error.defect_description: A team misses the cut-off and posts after the subledger close.

evidence.note: APQC advises identifying reconciliations and entries that can be done before month end; the checklist approach is common practice. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Run the lease system month-end batch
steps.description: Overnight the lease system closes the period: it recognises finance income on each finance lease, depreciates operating lease assets, amortises initial direct costs, ages receivables and builds the month-end subledger reports and the ledger interface.

error.defect_description: None introduced; data errors from the month pass through.

evidence.note: Finance income at a constant periodic rate on the net investment and straight-line operating lease income follow IFRS 16 as summarised by BDO; batch timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Close payables and list accruals
steps.description: Accounts payable and ledger clerks post supplier invoices received up to the cut-off, list services received but not invoiced (legal, bailiff, transport, software) from purchase orders and e-mails to department heads, and reconcile the payables subledger to the ledger.

error.defect_description: An unbilled service is missed from the accrual list.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: expense cut-off

evidence.note: Wait covers the morning after the batch and, at the high end, a weekend. Team hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile the lease subledger to the ledger
steps.description: Lease accountants tie the month-end subledger reports to the ledger control accounts: net investment in finance leases, unearned income, residuals, operating lease assets and depreciation, receivables by aging bucket, unapplied cash and security deposits. They list every difference with its cause.

error.defect_description: A difference is explained away as timing when it is a booking or interface error.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: monthly subledger-to-ledger reconciliation

evidence.note: Monthly reconciliation of subsidiary systems to the ledger from two independent sources, with a second reviewer, as described in Cornell's reconciliation narrative. Team hours and difference rate are author estimates for a 55,000-contract portfolio.

steps.name: Research and correct differences
steps.description: The lease accountant traces each difference to contracts and postings (a contract booked with the wrong accounting class, an interface line rejected, a payout not terminated, a write-off posted only in the ledger), asks operations to fix the lease system and drafts the correcting entry, then re-checks the reconciliation.

error.defect_description: Correcting entry posted to the wrong account or period.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile bank accounts
steps.description: The ledger clerks reconcile each bank account (operating, lockbox, debit collection, payroll and the securitisation collection and reserve accounts) to the ledger, list outstanding items and clear stale ones.

error.defect_description: A reconciling item is carried forward without follow-up.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: monthly bank reconciliation

evidence.note: APQC data put the median at four hours to reconcile one bank account (top performers 2.6 hours). About eight accounts are assumed.

steps.name: Reconcile other balance sheet accounts
steps.description: The clerks reconcile prepaid expenses, deposits, fixed assets of the company's own premises and equipment, clearing and suspense accounts, payroll liabilities and sundry receivables, attaching support and listing items to clear.

error.defect_description: A suspense balance is left uncleared.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: balance sheet account reconciliations

evidence.note: Asset and liability accounts reconciled monthly or by risk, as in Cornell's narrative. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile securitisation and bank debt
steps.description: A lease accountant ties the securitisation liability for each conduit and the credit facility balance to funder and bank statements and treasury's records, accrues interest and amortises financing fees by the effective interest method, and checks the cash reserve accounts.

error.defect_description: Interest accrual uses the wrong rate reset or a pool sold late in the month is missed.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: reconciliation of securitisation and bank debt to third-party statements

next.condition: difference with treasury or the funder

evidence.note: Contracts sold to conduits stay on the balance sheet with a securitisation liability (organisation file assumption). Funder statements arrive on about business day 2 or 3 while the clerks are still on bank and other reconciliations, so little extra wait is shown. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Resolve funding differences with treasury
steps.description: The securitisation and funding analyst works out differences between the ledger and the conduit or bank figures (pool cut timing, collections remitted, fees) and agrees the correcting entry with the lease accountant.

error.defect_description: Difference agreed without the funder confirming it.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Tie in loss allowance and lease accounting entries
steps.description: The lease accountant checks that the IFRS 9 expected credit loss allowance and the month's lease accounting entries from the lease and credit loss accounting process are posted, that the allowance roll-forward ties to write-offs and recoveries, and that the charge is reasonable against delinquency.

error.defect_description: Allowance roll-forward does not tie and the gap is booked to the charge.

evidence.note: IFRS 9 impairment applies to lease receivables (BDO summary of IFRS 16). Waiting for the allowance on about business day 3 or 4 overlaps with other reconciliation work, so little extra wait is shown; author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare accruals and other journal entries
steps.description: Lease accountants prepare the month's manual entries with support: payables accruals from the clerks' list, payroll, bonus and commission accruals, deferred broker fees, professional fees, prepaid amortisation, and the sales tax payable true-up agreed with the tax team.

error.defect_description: Accrual duplicated or reversed twice.

evidence.note: Author estimate of entries and hours.

steps.name: Approve manual journal entries
steps.description: The accounting manager reviews each manual entry above the threshold against its support and approves it in the ledger, or sends it back to the preparer, who fixes it the same day; the preparer cannot approve their own entry.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: manual journal entries approved by someone other than the preparer

next.condition: approved, with returned entries fixed and re-approved the same day

evidence.note: Second-person review as a key control, as in Cornell's narrative. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Review and sign off reconciliations
steps.description: The accounting managers review the subledger, bank, debt and balance sheet reconciliations, question aged reconciling items and unexplained differences, and sign each one off or return it.

error.defect_description: A weak explanation is accepted.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: independent review and sign-off of reconciliations

evidence.note: Preparer and reviewer must differ (Cornell). Return rate and hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Run the trial balance and consolidate
steps.description: The financial reporting analyst runs the preliminary trial balance, combines the operating company with the securitisation and warehouse entities it consolidates, and eliminates balances between them.

error.defect_description: Elimination missed after a new pool entity is added.

evidence.note: APQC measures the close from running the trial balance to completing consolidated statements. Hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Analyse variances
steps.description: The analyst compares each balance and income line with last month and budget, asks accountants, treasury and operations to explain movements above the threshold (bookings, delinquency, funding costs) and writes the commentary.

error.defect_description: A real error is explained as volume.

evidence.note: APQC notes most barriers to a faster close come down to data quality. Error rate and hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Draft the financial statements
steps.description: The analyst updates the statement templates (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, allowance roll-forward, funding and portfolio notes) and the lender key-figures schedule from the consolidated trial balance.

error.defect_description: A link in the statement template points to the wrong account range.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Controller reviews the draft
steps.description: The controller reads the draft statements and commentary, challenges the allowance, residual and accrual judgements, checks the close checklist is complete and either accepts the draft or lists adjustments.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: management review of the financial statements

evidence.note: Author estimate; the high end of the wait covers a weekend.

steps.name: Post late adjustments and redraft
steps.description: A lease accountant posts the adjustments from the review, the analyst reruns the trial balance and updates the statements and commentary.

error.defect_description: Statement not refreshed after the adjustment.

next.condition: minor change, straight to the CFO

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: CFO approves release
steps.description: The chief financial officer reviews the statements, the main variances and covenant-sensitive figures and approves release to the chief executive, treasury for lender reporting and planning for the management report, or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Credit facility reporting covenants (monthly statements certified by a responsible officer within about 20 to 30 days) and the company's delegation of authority

evidence.note: Sample credit agreement clauses set monthly statements 20 to 30 days after month end, certified by a responsible officer. Timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Lock the period and complete the checklist
steps.description: The accounting manager closes the period in the ledger and the lease system so nothing more posts, checks that every checklist task and reconciliation is signed off and filed for the auditors, and notes late items for next month.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: period lock and evidence of completed close tasks

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Distribute the statements
steps.description: The financial reporting analyst sends the approved statements to planning for the management report, to treasury for the borrowing base and covenant calculations and to tax, and files them for the auditors.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Organisation file sends financial statements to covenant reporting, management reporting, the annual audit, income tax and budgeting.

steps.name: Prepare the quarter-end package
steps.description: At quarter end the accounting manager adds the schedules the lenders, the board and the auditors need: covenant inputs, detailed notes, the quarterly review of lower-risk reconciliations and the auditors' interim requests.

error.defect_description: Schedule figures not tied back to the statements.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Post a correcting entry from variance analysis
steps.description: When a movement turns out to be a missing, duplicated or misposted entry, a lease accountant drafts the correcting entry with support and updates the affected reconciliation.

error.defect_description: Correction posted to the wrong account.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Approve the correcting entry
steps.description: The accounting manager checks the correcting entry and its support and approves it in the ledger so the analyst can rerun the trial balance and continue drafting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: manual journal entries approved by someone other than the preparer

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Rework a returned reconciliation
steps.description: The preparer clears the reviewer's points on a returned reconciliation: documents or writes off aged reconciling items, explains or corrects differences and updates the support.

error.defect_description: Aged item written off without approval.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Re-review the reconciliation
steps.description: The accounting manager checks that each review point on the returned reconciliation is cleared and the support is complete, and signs the reconciliation off.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting expected by the external auditor and relied on in lender and conduit reporting: independent review and sign-off of reconciliations

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Subledger differences
exceptions.description: The lease subledger does not agree with the ledger; accountants trace contracts and postings, operations fixes the lease system and the reconciliation is redone.

exceptions.name: Funding differences
exceptions.description: Securitisation or bank balances differ from funder or bank statements and treasury resolves the difference.

exceptions.name: Reconciliation returned by the reviewer
exceptions.description: The manager returns a reconciliation with aged or unexplained items.

exceptions.name: Error found in variance analysis
exceptions.description: A movement cannot be explained and turns out to be a missing or duplicated entry.

exceptions.name: Review adjustments
exceptions.description: The controller or the CFO asks for adjustments and the statements are redrafted.

exceptions.name: Quarter end
exceptions.description: Lender, board and auditor schedules are added after the statements are approved.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the last day of the month to approved statements
benchmarks.population: Monthly close at a mid-size independent lessor (derived)

evidence.note: Derived from the organisation file's 'about eight business days', which is about 11 calendar days. For comparison, APQC's median is 6.4 calendar days and its bottom quartile 10 or more (measured from running the trial balance), and in 2019 Ventana found 61% of companies close within six business days, so this lessor sits in the slower group, as spreadsheet-based finance companies with securitisation reporting often do.

benchmarks.population: About 2,300 organisations in APQC's general accounting survey (2018)
Ventana Research Office of Finance benchmark, 2019

evidence.note: 88% of companies with substantial automation close within six business days.
Sample clauses, mostly US; the lessor's own agreements were not seen.

pain_points.description: Differences between the lease system and the ledger are traced contract by contract in spreadsheets, and often start with booking or interface errors made earlier in the month.

evidence.note: APQC attributes most close delays to data quality; the lessor-specific cause is author judgement.

pain_points.description: Funder and bank statements, treasury schedules and the credit loss allowance arrive on business days 2 to 4, so the debt reconciliations and the allowance tie-in wait on other teams.

evidence.note: Author judgement.

pain_points.description: Manual journal entries and reconciliations queue for the two accounting managers, who also review lease accounting.

evidence.note: Author judgement.

pain_points.description: Late adjustments from the controller and CFO reviews force redrafts close to the lender deadline.

evidence.note: Lender deadlines from sample clauses; frequency of redrafts is author judgement.

sources.title: Metric of the month: cycle time for monthly close
sources.supports: APQC general accounting survey of 2,300 organisations: top quartile closes in 4.8 calendar days or less, median 6.4, bottom quartile 10 or more, measured from running the trial balance to consolidated statements; most barriers come down to data quality; do reconciliations and entries before month end where possible.

sources.title: Finally, a faster close
sources.supports: 2019 Office of Finance benchmark: 61% of participants close monthly within six business days (53% in 2015); 88% of companies with substantial automation do; 69% of those automating reconciliations versus 53% that do not.

sources.title: What bank reconciliation cycle time really tells you: metric of the month
sources.supports: APQC data: top performers reconcile a single bank account in about 2.6 hours, the median in four hours, bottom performers five hours or more.

sources.title: Transaction cycle narrative: account reconciliations and monitoring
sources.publisher: Cornell University, Division of Financial Services
sources.supports: Subsidiary systems reconciled to the ledger monthly from two independent sources; asset and liability accounts reconciled monthly or by risk; key control is a second reviewer's approval; key risk is late reconciliations.

sources.title: Monthly financial statements; compliance certificates (sample clauses)
sources.supports: Sample credit agreement clauses requiring monthly financial statements and compliance certificates 20 to 30 days after month end, certified by a responsible officer.

sources.title: IFRS 16 (accounting news, October 2018)
sources.supports: Lessor accounting unchanged from IAS 17: finance lease net investment with finance income at a constant periodic rate; operating lease income straight-line; IFRS 9 impairment applies to lease receivables.

sources.title: Wages for financial auditors and accountants (NOC 11100)
sources.supports: Hourly wages 2023-2024: Ontario low $24.73, median $40.87, high $72.12; Toronto region median $41.34.

sources.title: Wages for accounting and related clerks (NOC 14200)
sources.supports: Hourly wages 2023-2024: Ontario low $18.12, median $25.00, high $37.00.

assumptions: One case is one monthly close. Hands-on minutes are team hours (about 190 to 220 hours a month in total); the simulator adds them in sequence, so its median of about 14.5 days runs above the 11-day benchmark even though reconciliations, accruals and debt work run side by side; waits that overlap with other people's work (funder statements, the allowance) are shown as short.
Stated FTE (about 3 in total) is higher than the FTE implied by the modelled steps because close coordination, meetings, audit queries and small reconciliations are not modelled as steps.

The IFRS 9 allowance and lease accounting entries are produced by the separate account-for-leases-and-credit-losses process and only tied in here; sales tax returns are prepared by file-sales-taxes and only the payable true-up is booked here.
Securitised contracts stay on the balance sheet with a securitisation liability, as the organisation file assumes; the entities consolidated are assumed to be a warehouse trust and pool entities.

The lessor is private, so no statutory ICFR certification applies; controls are those the external auditor tests and lenders and conduits rely on. Lender reporting deadlines are taken from sample clauses, not the lessor's own agreements.

Organisation file note: the close-the-month process lists no link to report-to-securitisation-funders, although conduit reporting in practice uses closed balances; this workflow does not add that link.
